'''Mikaela Iacobelli''' is an Italian mathematician working in kinetic theory and partial differential equations.
She has been an Associate Professor of Mathematics at [[ETH Zurich]] since 2023.<ref name="appointment">{{cite web
 |title=24 new professors appointed at ETH Zurich and EPFL
 |url=https://ethrat.ch/en/appointments-march-23/
 |website=ETH Board
 |date=10 March 2023
}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Iacobelli earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 2009 and a master's degree ''cum laude'' in mathematics in 2012, both from the [[Sapienza University of Rome]].<ref name="ethcv">{{cite web
 |title=Short CV
 |url=https://people.math.ethz.ch/~imikaela/about
 |website=ETH Zurich
}}</ref>

She received a joint Ph.D. from [[Sapienza University of Rome]] and the [[École Polytechnique]] in 2015 under the supervision of Emanuele Caglioti and [[François Golse]]. Her thesis was titled ''Dynamics of large particle systems''.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Mikaela Iacobelli
 |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=195923
 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project
}}</ref>

From 2015 to 2017, she was a research associate at the [[University of Cambridge]]. She was an assistant professor at [[Durham University]] from 2017 to 2019, and a titular professor at [[ETH Zurich]] from 2019 to 2023. In 2023, she was appointed associate professor at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="appointment"/>

During the 2024–2025 academic year, she was a [[Von Neumann Fellow]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey.<ref name="ias">{{cite web
 |title=Mikaela Iacobelli
 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/mikaela-iacobelli
 |website=Institute for Advanced Study
}}</ref>

== Research ==

Iacobelli's research lies at the intersection of kinetic theory, plasma physics, statistical mechanics, and nonlinear partial differential equations. Her work studies the mathematical structures underlying singular limits, long-time dynamics, and degenerate problems.<ref name="ethprofile">{{cite web
 |title=Prof. Dr. Mikaela Iacobelli
 |url=https://people.math.ethz.ch/~imikaela/
 |website=ETH Zurich
}}</ref>

Her research topics include [[Vlasov equation|Vlasov-type equations]], quasineutral limits, kinetic [[Wasserstein metric|Wasserstein distances]], [[Landau damping]], magnetic and electromagnetic plasma models, quantization of measures, and ultrafast diffusion.<ref name="ethprofile"/> Her SNSF-funded project, ''Challenges and Breakthroughs in the Mathematics of Plasmas'', focuses on kinetic models and singular limits for magnetized and electromagnetic plasma systems.<ref name="snsfproject">{{cite web
 |title=Challenges and Breakthroughs in the Mathematics of Plasmas
 |url=https://data.snf.ch/grants/grant/226018
 |website=SNSF Data Portal
 |publisher=Swiss National Science Foundation
}}</ref>

== Professional service ==
Iacobelli is a member of the Committee for Women in Mathematics of the [[European Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Women in Mathematics Committee
 |url=https://euromathsoc.org/committee-women
 |website=European Mathematical Society
}}</ref> She is also a member of the standing committee of [[European Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Standing Committee
 |url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/about-us/organization/standing-commitee/
 |website=European Women in Mathematics
}}</ref>
